clue.text: Offshoots born on farms

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for born, as in genealogies
ranches are large farms, especially cattle farms

explanation.surface: Some new branches of a family were born out on the farms.
explanation.definitionFit: Branches are shoots growing out from a tree's trunk, so offshoots in the plant sense.

clue.text: Machine which is like nothing in existence

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for nothing goes inside the word for existence

parts.note: being means existence, as in 'come into being'
O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing on a contraption unlike anything that exists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which is like' is just a link: O looks like nothing (a zero), and it sits inside BEING.
explanation.definitionFit: Boeing is the American aircraft maker, and its airliners are called by its name, so a flying machine.

clue.text: Temporary performance

definitions.meaning: standing in for now, as in an interim chairman
the work of playing a part on stage or screen

explanation.surface: A stand-in role in a stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: An acting manager holds the post only for now; acting is also the craft of performing on stage.

clue.text: The team would be different if drink were banned

definitions.text: The team would be different if drink were banned

parts.words: The team would be different if drink were banned
parts.note: the name of a London football club, read as hiding a word for drink: take the drink out and the name would be another word altogether

explanation.surface: A football club's fortunes after a ban on alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a remark about players' drinking, but it points at a football club whose name ends in a word for drink, the sea being 'the drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chelsea is a London football club, so a team in the English league.

clue.text: Place where you are up above a bit of ancient writing

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second
in a down entry 'up' means the word for you is written bottom to top

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
OT, the Old Testament, is a part of ancient scripture

explanation.surface: A spot where you stand over an inscription from antiquity.
explanation.walkthrough: An EYOT is a small river island, as on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot is a small island in a river, so a particular spot or location.

clue.text: Being employed for the morning, provided entertainment

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning
used means put to work or employed

explanation.surface: Someone hired for the morning shift who kept everyone entertained.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused here is a past verb: to amuse is to divert or entertain someone.

clue.text: Lost blood after animal was hung up and appeared mottled

indicators.note: after puts the blood-losing piece behind the animal in the answer
in a down entry, hung up means the animal's word is written upwards

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, an animal
bled means lost blood

explanation.surface: A grim butcher's tale: the carcass hung up, drained of blood, looked streaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was hung up' turns RAM to MAR; BLED then follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Marbled describes a surface streaked or veined like marble, so blotched or mottled.

clue.text: Chant about a unit of electrical power, needed for striking quickly

indicators.note: about means the word for chant goes around the unit of power

parts.note: to chant is to sing
the watt is the SI unit of power

explanation.surface: A singing electrician needs a burst of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Swatting is hitting sharply, as one slaps at a fly with a quick blow.

clue.text: House type puts unusual chat into action

indicators.note: into means the rearranged letters go inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an act or action

indicators.note: unusual signals that the letters of chat are rearranged

explanation.surface: An estate agent's banter about a property type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes TACH from CHAT, and 'into' puts it inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A detached house stands alone, sharing no wall with a neighbour, a standard estate-agent category.

clue.text: In the trade centre a drinker gets back after about ten

indicators.note: after places the drinker's piece behind the turned number
about here means the letters of the number word are moved around
gets back means the word for drinker is written backwards

parts.note: a toper is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker returns to the market after ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges TEN to ENT and 'gets back' turns TOPER to REPOT: ENT + REPOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrepot is a port or warehouse town where goods are imported and re-exported, a hub of commerce.

clue.text: Almost sincere and industrious one becomes absentee

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for sincere is dropped

parts.note: true means sincere, as in a true friend
the ant is proverbially hardworking

explanation.surface: An honest hard worker who nonetheless starts skipping work.
explanation.definitionFit: A truant is a pupil who stays away from school without permission, so one who is absent.

clue.text: Workshop put right after untruth follows goddess

indicators.note: follows means the untruth comes after the goddess
after means right comes behind the untruth

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin
a lie is an untruth

explanation.surface: Setting a workshop straight after someone tells a lie about a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: ATE, the Greek goddess of mischief, is a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a working room.

clue.text: The burden of unemployment is in the Newcastle area

indicators.note: is in means the burden word sits inside the area letters

parts.note: NE, the North East of England, is where Newcastle stands
an onus is a burden or responsibility

explanation.surface: A gloomy line about joblessness weighing on Tyneside.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-use is a state of not being used, so being out of employment in the sense of a thing left idle.

clue.text: In the story the man is about fifty but vigorous

indicators.note: In means the inner piece is put inside the word for the story

parts.note: the attic is the top storey of a house (story in American spelling)

indicators.note: is about means the word for the man goes around the fifty

parts.note: he refers to a man
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A tale about a fifty-year-old who is still sprightly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'story' looks like a tale but is a floor of a house, the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: Athletic means physically strong and energetic, fit for sport.

clue.text: Letter written with pen and oils

indicators.note: written suggests the letters of pen and oils are worked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Writing a letter with a pen and painting in oils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written' signals the anagram of PEN and OILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Is allowed to go punting and have a ball -a springtime activity

parts.note: may means is permitted
to pole is to push a punt along with a pole
to dance is what you do at a ball

explanation.surface: Permission to go punting on the river and then party: a perfect spring day.
explanation.walkthrough: A punt is a flat boat pushed along with a long pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Dancing around a beribboned pole is a traditional English May Day custom.

clue.text: Be apathetic about a doctrine in a depressing way

indicators.note: about means the word for be apathetic goes round the doctrine

parts.note: to dally is to dawdle without energy
an ism is any doctrine or creed

explanation.surface: Being indifferent towards a creed in a gloomy manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismally means gloomily or miserably, so causing low spirits.

clue.text: Punishment given with a nine-inch ruler?

parts.note: a span is a measure of nine inches, a hand's stretch
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A teacher punishing a pupil with a measuring rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick, which suits a school beating, but it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanking is a smacking given as a chastisement.

clue.text: Perhaps meet in prince a presumption

indicators.note: Perhaps hints the letters of the phrase are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: Meeting a royal might be thought a cheeky assumption.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals the anagram of MEET IN PRINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Impertinence is cheeky boldness, the sense of presumption meaning overstepping one's place.

clue.text: Feels sorry for birds seen on a little river

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for river
egrets are white herons

explanation.surface: Someone pitying the herons on a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: To regret something is to feel sorry about it.

clue.text: To put an end to lawlessness, make war

indicators.note: end to means the small word is put at the tail of the word for lawlessness

parts.note: crime is lawlessness

explanation.surface: A call to arms to stamp out crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To put an end to' tells us AN goes at the end of CRIME; 'make war' means the answer makes a war's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Crimean War of 1853 to 1856 was fought by Britain, France and Turkey against Russia.

clue.text: Twins employed in strange ministries

indicators.note: employed in means the letters are found used inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Twins working in odd government departments.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini is the zodiac sign of the Twins, Castor and Pollux.

clue.text: Prison camp into which a worthless person comes without gratitude

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the person's word wraps around the thanks

parts.note: slag is slang for a worthless person
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A thankless rogue being sent into a prison camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp in the Second World War.

clue.text: A doctor has fortune after a drink, but he can only speak the same language

definitions.text: he can only speak the same language

indicators.note: after says the fortune word comes behind the drink

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
nog is a strong beer or eggnog
a lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: A doctor gets lucky over a drink, though he speaks no foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: A monoglot is a person who knows only one tongue.

clue.text: Turn aside and start turning after the drive is seen to be in disrepair

indicators.note: after puts the first letter behind the jumbled drive
in disrepair means the letters of drive are broken up and rearranged
start means the first letter of turning

explanation.surface: Diverting traffic because the road is broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in disrepair' makes DIVER from DRIVE; 'start turning' gives T after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert is to deflect or redirect something from its course.

clue.text: The summons caught everyone

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A summons that catches everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A call is a summons, a demand to come.

clue.text: Linger when it is discovered among unusual lore

indicators.note: discovered among means the small word is found inside the jumbled letters
unusual signals the letters of lore are rearranged

explanation.surface: Lingering when something odd turns up in folklore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' makes LOER from LORE, and IT goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter is to hang about idly.

clue.text: Marry and get back home: that's the stuff

parts.note: to mate is to pair up or marry

indicators.note: get back means the word for home is written backwards

parts.note: a lair is an animal's home

explanation.surface: Get married and go home: that's the way of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Material is cloth or matter, the substance things are made of.

clue.text: Love soldiers in my retreat for ascetic practice

indicators.note: in means the love-and-soldiers piece goes inside the turned word
retreat means the word my is turned backwards

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Love and troops in my hideaway for a life of self-denial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a hideaway, but it turns MY to YM.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogism is the discipline of yoga, an austere spiritual practice.

clue.text: Caught joining up and making a ringing noise

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
linking means connecting or joining up

explanation.surface: Caught in the act of joining up, with a clatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinking is the light ringing sound of glasses or coins knocking.
